== Places of Worship ==

{{Anchors|General Places of Worship}}
{{Anchors|Imperial Mausoleums}}
In Japan, a place of worship ({{nihongo|haisho|はいしょ}}) refers to a designated area for veneration in front of sacred sites. Many {{ill|Japanese imperial tombs|en|Japanese imperial tombs|qid=Q17218816|lt=Japanese imperial tombs}} and {{ill|Kofun|ca|Kofun|cs|Kofun|da|Kofun|de|Kofun|eo|Kofun|es|Kofun|fa|کوفون|fi|Kofun|fr|Kofun|he|קופון (רוגם)|hr|Kofun (grobnica)|it|Kofun|ja|古墳|ko|고훈|my|ခိုဖွန်း|pl|Kofun (kurhan)|pt|Kofun|ru|Кофун (захоронение)|simple|Kofun|th|โคฟุง|tr|Kofun|uk|Кофун|zh|古墳|qid=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} include places of worship. At shrines, the {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|en|Haiden (Shinto)|qid=Q3125745|lt=Haiden (Shinto)}} often serves this role, but in some cases, such as {{ill|Suwa-taisha|en|Suwa-taisha|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha}}, both a place of worship and a haiden exist<ref group="gm">Place of Worship at Suwa Taisha（{{googlemap|諏訪大社拝所}}）.</ref>.<ref>https://www.nihongomaster.com/japanese/dictionary/word/62653/haisho-%E9%85%8D%E6%89%80-%E3%81%AF%E3%81%84%E3%81%97%E3%82%87</ref>
== Haisho ==
{{Anchors|Haisho (Haijo)|Haijo|General Haisho in Japan}}
{{Anchors|Characteristics (Haijo)|Overview (Haijo)}}
In general Japanese terminology, a "Haisho" (はいしょ<ref name="Japanese Dictionary"/>/{{Citation needed|はいじょ|date=April 2024}}) refers to a designated place for worship in front of a sacred area.

Many {{ill|Japanese imperial tombs|en|Japanese imperial tombs|qid=Q17218816|lt=Japanese imperial tombs}}, Empress' tombs, and designated {{ill|Tombs|ja|陵墓|lt=Imperial tomb}} (including {{ill|Kofun|ca|Kofun|cs|Kofun|da|Kofun|de|Kofun|eo|Kofun|es|Kofun|fa|کوفون|fi|Kofun|fr|Kofun|he|קופון (רוגם)|hr|Kofun (grobnica)|it|Kofun|ja|古墳|ko|고훈|my|ခိုဖွန်း|pl|Kofun (kurhan)|pt|Kofun|ru|Кофун (захоронение)|simple|Kofun|th|โคฟุง|tr|Kofun|uk|Кофун|zh|古墳|qid=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}}) feature haisho. In the case of {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrines}}, the {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|en|Haiden (Shinto)|qid=Q3125745|lt=Haiden (Shinto)}} serves a similar function as a larger facility, meaning some shrines lack a dedicated haisho. However, some, like {{ill|Suwa-taisha|en|Suwa-taisha|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha}}, include both<ref group="gm">Haisho at Suwa Taisha（{{googlemap|Suwa Taisha Haisho}}）.</ref>, while others, like the {{ill|Hachidai Ryuo Haisho|ja|八大竜王拝所|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135504585}} of {{ill|Tsukubusuma Shrine|en|Tsukubusuma Shrine|qid=Q11643470|lt=Tsukubusuma Shrine}} (worshiping the {{ill|Eight Great Dragon Kings|ja|八大竜王|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11390736}} in {{ill|Lake Biwa|en|Lake Biwa|qid=Q200239|lt=Lake Biwa}}), only feature a haisho<ref name="Hachidai Ryuo Haisho" group="gm" />.<ref group="note">The main deity of Tsukubusuma Shrine has a honden but no haiden, and the Hachidai Ryuo has neither a honden nor a haiden.</ref>

Additionally, a haisho situated far from its worship target is known as a "Remote Worship Place" ({{ill|Haisho|ja|遥拝所|lt=Yōhaijo}}), designed for worshiping from a distance.

Since the Meiji era, imperial mausoleums and empress' tombs often include different types of haisho: '''General Haisho''' for common worshippers, '''Special Haisho''' for authorized individuals, and '''Imperial Haisho''' (御拝所, Gohai-jo) reserved for the emperor or the emperor and empress.<ref group="宮内庁">{{Cite web|url=https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/kunaicho/koho/goryou/pdf/image.pdf |title=Imperial Tomb Image Guide |format=PDF |work=Official Website |publisher=Imperial Household Agency |accessdate=2019-06-01 }}</ref>

==Yōhaijo==

The term "遥拝所" (yōhaijo) refers to a "remote worship site" in Japanese culture. It is a designated place where individuals can worship or pay respects to a sacred site, such as a shrine or temple, from a distance. This practice is particularly significant when direct access to the sacred site is challenging due to geographical obstacles or other restrictions.

An example of a yōhaijo is the one associated with the {{ill|Kawaguchi Sengen Shrine|ja|河口浅間神社}} near Lake Kawaguchi. This remote worship site allows visitors to honor Mount Fuji, which is considered sacred in Shinto belief, without ascending the mountain itself. The site features a torii gate framing a view of Mount Fuji, providing a symbolic connection for worshippers. <ref>https://huannntravel.com/fujisan-torii-kawaguchiko/</ref>

In summary, a yōhaijo serves as a meaningful location for individuals to engage in worship or reflection directed toward a distant sacred place, maintaining spiritual practices even when physical proximity is not possible.

== Uganju ==
{{Anchors|Haisho (Uganju)|Uganju|Okinawan Haisho}}
A "Haisho" (うがんじゅ, うがん) in the {{ill|Ryukyu Islands|ja|琉球諸島|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10905515}} and {{ill|Amami Islands|az|Amami adaları|ceb|Amami Shotō|cs|Amami (souostroví)|de|Amami-Inseln|eo|Amamioj|es|Islas Amami|eu|Amami uharteak|fa|جزایر آمامی|fi|Amamisaaret|fr|Îles Amami|gl|Illas Amami|id|Kepulauan Amami|it|Isole Amami|ja|奄美群島|ko|아마미 군도|lt|Amami salos|nl|Amami-eilanden|no|Amamiøyene|pt|Ilhas Amami|ro|Insulele Amami|ru|Амами (острова)|simple|Amami Islands|sn|Zvitsuwa zve Amami|sv|Amamiöarna|th|หมู่เกาะอามามิ|tr|Amami Adaları|uk|Амамі (острови)|vi|Quần đảo Amami|wuu|奄美群岛|zh|奄美群島|zh_min_nan|Amami Kûn-tó|zh_yue|奄美群島|qid=Q453510|lt=Amami Islands}} refers to a site where deities are enshrined and worshiped.

These places are often regarded as sacred areas where deities reside{{r|kb}}, and compared to {{ill|Ontake|en|Ontake|qid=Q11071176|lt=Utaki}}, they are smaller in scale and involve fewer individuals in their rituals{{r|kb}}. Some also refer to capes where {{ill|visiting god|ja|来訪神|fr|lt=Visiting deities|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q30925139}} are believed to have arrived{{r|kb}}.

=== Naming ===
{{Anchors|Naming (Uganju)}}
The standard kanji for "Uganju" is "拝所", but the alternate spelling "御願所" can also be found<ref name="Okinawa Encyclopedia_1">{{Harvnb|Okinawa Encyclopedia|1983|loc=Volume 1, p. 279}}</ref>. In northern {{ill|Okinawa Island|af|Okinawa-eilande|ang|Ocinawa|ar|جزيرة أوكيناوا|az|Okinava|be|Акінава|bg|Окинава (остров)|bs|Okinawa|ca|Illa d'Okinawa|ceb|Okinawa (pulo)|cs|Okinawa|cv|Окинава|cy|Ynys Okinawa|da|Okinawa (ø)|de|Okinawa Hontō|el|Οκινάουα|eo|Okinava insulo|es|Isla de Okinawa|et|Okinawa|eu|Okinawa (uhartea)|fa|جزیره اوکیناوا|fi|Okinawa|fr|Île Okinawa|gl|Illa de Okinawa|haw|Okinawa Nui|he|אוקינאווה (אי)|hr|Okinawa|hu|Okinava (sziget)|hy|Օկինավա կղզի|iba|Pulau Okinawa|id|Pulau Okinawa|it|Isola di Okinawa|ja|沖縄本島|ka|ოკინავა|kk|Окинава (арал)|km|កោះអូគីណាវ៉ា|kn|ಓಕಿನಾವ|ko|오키나와섬|ku|Girava Okinawayê|ky|Окинава|la|Okinawa|lt|Okinavos sala|lv|Okinava (sala)|mk|Окинава|ms|Pulau Okinawa|nl|Okinawa (eiland)|nn|Okinawa|no|Okinawa|oc|Okinawa|os|Окинавæ|pl|Okinawa (wyspa)|pt|Ilha de Okinawa|ro|Insula Okinawa|ru|Окинава|sc|Okinawa|sh|Okinawa|si|ඔකිනාවා දූපත|simple|Okinawa|sk|Okinava (ostrov)|sl|Okinava|sn|Chitsuwa che Okinawa|sq|Okinava|sr|Окинава|sv|Okinawa|ta|ஓக்கினாவா தீவு|th|เกาะโอกินาวะ|tl|Pulo ng Okinawa|tok|ma Okinawa|tr|Okinawa Adası|uk|Окінава (острів)|ur|جزیرہ اوکیناوا|vi|Okinawa (đảo)|war|Okinawa (purô)|wuu|冲绳岛|zh|沖繩島|zh_min_nan|Okinawa Tó|zh_yue|沖繩島|qid=Q600614|lt=Okinawa Island}}, "Uganju" is also known as "Ugami," while in the {{ill|Amami Islands|az|Amami adaları|ceb|Amami Shotō|cs|Amami (souostroví)|de|Amami-Inseln|eo|Amamioj|es|Islas Amami|eu|Amami uharteak|fa|جزایر آمامی|fi|Amamisaaret|fr|Îles Amami|gl|Illas Amami|id|Kepulauan Amami|it|Isole Amami|ja|奄美群島|ko|아마미 군도|lt|Amami salos|nl|Amami-eilanden|no|Amamiøyene|pt|Ilhas Amami|ro|Insulele Amami|ru|Амами (острова)|simple|Amami Islands|sn|Zvitsuwa zve Amami|sv|Amamiöarna|th|หมู่เกาะอามามิ|tr|Amami Adaları|uk|Амамі (острови)|vi|Quần đảo Amami|wuu|奄美群岛|zh|奄美群島|zh_min_nan|Amami Kûn-tó|zh_yue|奄美群島|qid=Q453510|lt=Amami Islands}}, it is called "Ugami-yama" (拝み山), representing an older phonetic form{{r|Okinawa Encyclopedia_1}}. In the {{ill|Yaeyama Islands|en|Yaeyama Islands|qid=Q696496|lt=Yaeyama Islands}}, phonetic variations derived from "Ogami" (拝み) include "On" in {{ill|Ishigaki Island|en|Ishigaki Island|qid=Q714339|lt=Ishigaki}}, {{ill|Taketomi Island|arz|تاكيتومى (جزيره)|az|Taketomi|ceb|Taketomi-shima (pulo sa Hapon)|cs|Taketomi|de|Taketomi-jima|es|Taketomi|fa|جزیره تاکه‌تومی|fr|Taketomi-jima|id|Pulau Taketomi|ja|竹富島|ko|다케토미섬|lt|Taketomis|mk|Такетоми (остров)|ms|Pulau Taketomi|pt|Ilha de Taketomi|ru|Такэтоми (остров)|sn|Chitsuwa che Taketomi|sv|Taketomi-jima|tr|Taketomi Adası|uk|Такетомі (острів)|uz|Taketomi oroli|vi|Taketomi|zh|竹富島|qid=Q474560|lt=Taketomi}}, and {{ill|Iriomote Island|ar|جزيرة إيريوموته|az|İriomote|ca|Illa d'Iriomote|ceb|Iriomote-jima|cs|Iriomote|de|Iriomote|eo|Iriomote|es|Isla Iriomote|fa|جزیره اریوموته|fi|Iriomote|fr|Iriomote-jima|gl|Iriomote|he|איריומוטה|hu|Iriomote|id|Pulau Iriomote|it|Iriomote|ja|西表島|ko|이리오모테섬|lt|Iriomotė|ms|Pulau Iriomote|nl|Iriomote (eiland)|pl|Iriomote|pt|Iriomote|ru|Ириомоте|simple|Iriomote Island|sv|Iriomote|th|อิริโอโมเตะ|tr|Iriomote Adası|uk|Іріомоте|vi|Iriomote-jima|zh|西表島|zh_min_nan|Iriomote-tó|qid=Q432124|lt=Iriomote}}; "Wan" in {{ill|Kuroshima|de|Kuroshima|ja|黒島|ko|구로시마섬|nl|Kuroshima|zh|黑島|qid=Q1207339|lt=Kuroshima, Okinawa}}, {{ill|Kohama Island|az|Kohama|ceb|Kohama Island|de|Kohama-jima|es|Kohama|fr|Kohama-jima|id|Pulau Kohama|ja|小浜島|ko|고하마섬|ru|Кохама|sn|Chitsuwa che Kohama|tr|Kohama Adası|uk|Кохама|vi|Kohama|zh|小濱島|qid=Q702603|lt=Kohama Island}}, and {{ill|Aragusuku Islands|az|Araqusuku|ceb|Aragusuku-jima|fr|Aragusuku-jima|ja|新城島|ko|아라구스쿠섬|ru|Арагусуку|sn|Zvitsuwa zve Aragusuku|tr|Aragusuku Adaları|uk|Араґусуку|uz|Aragusuku orollari|zh|新城島|qid=Q702414|lt=Aragusuku}}; and "Wa" in {{ill|Hateruma|az|Hateruma|ceb|Hateruma-jima|de|Hateruma|es|Hateruma|fr|Hateruma-jima|hu|Hateruma|id|Pulau Hateruma|ja|波照間島|ko|하테루마섬|lt|Hateruma|pt|Hateruma|ru|Хатерума|sn|Chitsuwa che Hateruma|sv|Hateruma-jima|tr|Hateruma Adası|uk|Хатерума|vi|Hateruma|zh|波照間島|qid=Q697600|lt=Hateruma Island}}<ref name="Okinawa Encyclopedia_1"/>. The word "Utaki" (御嶽) is a standard term{{r|Okinawa Encyclopedia_1}}, but colloquially, "Ugan," "Mui" (森, meaning "forest"), and "Yama" are also used{{r|Okinawa Encyclopedia_1}}.

=== Characteristics ===
{{Anchors|Characteristics (Uganju)|Overview (Uganju)}}
Haisho vary in form<ref name="Okinawa Encyclopedia_2">{{Harvnb|Okinawa Encyclopedia|1983|loc=Volume 2, p. 495}}</ref>. Generally, they are located in forests beneath tall trees, sometimes marked by stones (such as coral formations){{r|Okinawa Encyclopedia_2}}, while others have concrete structures{{r|Okinawa Encyclopedia_2}}. They are considered sacred spaces{{r|Okinawa Encyclopedia_2}}. Even Shinto shrines fall within the definition of haisho{{r|Okinawa Encyclopedia_2}}. Additionally, communal haisho can be found at various facilities, including elementary, middle, and high schools, though the {{ill|Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology|en|Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology|qid=Q1054379|lt=Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology}} does not classify these as religious institutions{{r|Okinawa Encyclopedia_2}}. On {{ill|Miyako Island|ar|جزيرة مياكو|arz|مياكو (جزيره)|az|Miyako adası|ceb|Miyako-jima|de|Miyako-jima|eo|Mijako (insulo)|es|Isla Miyako|fa|میاکو-جیما|fr|Miyako-jima|id|Pulau Miyako|it|Miyakojima (isola)|ja|宮古島|jv|Pulo Miyako|kk|Мияко (арал)|ko|미야코섬|lt|Mijakodžima|pt|Miyako-jima|ro|Miyako-jima|ru|Мияко (остров)|sc|Miyakojima (ìsula)|sv|Miyako-jima|tr|Miyako Adası|uk|Міяко (острів)|vi|Miyako-jima|wuu|宫古岛|zh|宮古島|zh_min_nan|Miiako-zima|zh_yue|宮古島|qid=Q700946|lt=Miyako Island}}, haisho may be dedicated to individual guardian deities{{r|Okinawa Encyclopedia_2}}, called "Maugan" (まうがん), with each person having a unique worship site{{r|Okinawa Encyclopedia_2}}.
